@graph.description:
Replication of nav2's drive-on-heading behavior system test
(nav2_system_tests/src/behaviors/drive_on_heading, main). Where upstream drives the
/drive_on_heading action with a Python tester (drive_tester.py) against a tb3
Gazebo world, this campaign runs the full nav2 stack (files/nav2_stack.launch.py,
the same hexagon world as the sibling behavior, error_codes and system_failure
campaigns) and drives /drive_on_heading with the generic action_call primitive.

MEANING OF A CELL: one configuration is one upstream drive_on_heading parameterization
(nav2_system_tests.csv lines 15-18, test case `test_drive_on_heading_behavior`). The
drive behavior SUCCEEDS after reaching the target point for the valid-costmap case,
and ABORTS for the costmap-dependent and impossible-command cases. The valid-costmap
cell carries expect_success: true; the invalid-costmap, impossible-command and
lethal-costmap cells carry expect_success: false. The analysis additionally verifies
the upstream `error_code == 0` assertion on success and the specific error_code on
abort from the recorded /drive_on_heading/_action timestamps (not expressible in the
scenario; see drive_on_heading_behavior.osc header).

PORTED CASE -> GOAL:
- Invalid costmap  (CSV line 15) -> speed 0.15, target x 0.15, time_allowance 5 s
- Valid costmap    (CSV line 16) -> speed 0.15, target x 0.15, time_allowance 5 s
- Impossible command (CSV line 17) -> speed 0.15, target x 0.15, time_allowance 0.1 s
- Lethal costmap   (CSV line 18) -> speed 0.15, target x 0.15, time_allowance 5 s

NOT PORTED: the preempt-with-faster-command and cancel sub-cases inside the upstream
valid-costmap test, and the manual costmap publishing used to trigger
costmap-dependent failures. A mid-run preempt or cancel cannot be sequenced in this
scenario framework (action_call has no preempt or cancel entry point --
RosActionCall.shutdown() cancels only at scenario teardown), the framework has no
mechanism to publish arbitrary costmaps to /local_costmap/costmap_raw before sending
the goal, and the upstream "impossible target sign" check is one of several
sub-assertions inside upstream's imperative Test C that cannot be split into
separately-graded scenario cells. Recorded, not faked, in readme.md.

UPSTREAM ODDITY worth recording: upstream CMakeLists.txt sets
BT_NAVIGATOR_XML=navigate_to_pose_w_replanning_and_behavior.xml, a file that exists
neither in the navigation2 source tree nor in the installed nav2_bt_navigator share
directory (verified in the robovast image). It is immaterial here -- /drive_on_heading
is a behavior-server action, not a BT node -- but the CSV row's BT column therefore
names a file that cannot be loaded.
